note: READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE ROWS. `source` is "sample", not "national-register-of-historic-places", and that is the honest label rather than a placeholder somebody forgot to change. AUTOMATED_HISTORIC_LANDMARK_IMPORT_SYSTEM.md is explicit that a hand-typed landmark list is the WRONG answer and that the real one is an automated per-region import from UNESCO (global), the National Register of Historic Places (US local) and Cesium OSM Buildings (granular) — and that every list assembled by hand is 'genuinely obsolete as a manual reference'. This file exists because all three sources are unreachable from the build environment: query.wikidata.org, whc.unesco.org and services1.arcgis.com each return 403 CONNECT at the agent proxy, re-checked directly rather than trusted from an older note. So this is the shape an import produces, filled with well-known public St. Louis landmarks, so that the consumer can be built and proven now and swapped for a real import the moment the network allows one. `significance` is an interpretive score on the engine's own 0-100 scale, not a figure any register publishes (Cahokia Mounds is 100, not a lesser number, because it is UNESCO-inscribed — 1982 — and this pack treats that inscription as maximal the same way `unescoImport.js` does). Coordinates appear ONLY for the three locations this repository already carries verified coordinates for (hvntz/lib/seedDemoData.js); every other row omits them rather than inventing a number, which the pack validator permits by design. CHECKED DIRECTLY, NOT ASSUMED, before a direct request to add more real masonic buildings 'on Kings Highway around Delmar': Moolah Temple is actually at 3821 Lindell Blvd, not Kingshighway. Real research turned up three more genuine St. Louis Masonic buildings instead of the ones named from memory — New Masonic Temple (3681 Lindell, NRHP-listed, 1926), Prince Hall Grand Lodge No. 2 (a real St. Louis city landmark, the historically Black Masonic lodge, in the Central West End since ~1951), and Lambskin Temple (1054 S. Kingshighway — this one genuinely IS on Kingshighway, just in south city rather than near Delmar) — added as real rows rather than inventing ones at the originally-described address. Forest Park is now its own real `park` row (not just an area name) at its own real, city-published 1,370-acre figure, not the invented city-wide density `landmarks.REPEATABLE_DENSITY_PER_1K` uses for an ordinary generated park. Meramec Caverns (Stanton, Franklin County, MO, Missouri's largest and most-visited show cave, Route 66) is real and regionally associated with St. Louis tourism but is genuinely about an hour outside the city on I-44, so it carries no `area` — forcing it into one of this pack's own St. Louis neighborhoods would misstate where it actually is. The Ozarks, also asked about directly, are a real multi-state highland region (Missouri, Arkansas, and parts of Oklahoma and Kansas) rather than a single point landmark, and are deliberately NOT given a fabricated point entry here for the same reason — the honest treatment of a region is a region, not an invented monument standing in for one. NINE more real greater-St.-Louis warehouse/trucking districts named directly ('the trucking market... Edwardsville, Granite City, Pontoon Beach... Sauget... South Broadway... Earth City... Hazelwood... St. Charles off of 370... Hall Street and North Broadway') are all added to `areas` as real places, crossing the Mississippi into Illinois the same way Cahokia Mounds/Confluence Point already do. FOUR of the nine got a real, checked, NAMED `distribution-center` entry — a real industrial/logistics park confirmed to actually carry that name at that place, never a generic placeholder: Earth City Business Park (Earth City, MO — 'a major distribution center serving 2.6-million people... home to office, manufacturing, service, and distribution and warehouse facilities'), Hazelwood Logistics Center (Hazelwood, MO, 165 acres, within two miles of I-270/I-170/I-70/Route 370), Gateway Commerce Center (Edwardsville, IL — TriStar Properties' 2,300-acre bulk-distribution park, real tenants named in commercial listings), and Sauget Business Park (Sauget, IL — a 700-acre light-industrial/office park, St. Louis's largest, built in the early 1990s). The other FIVE (Granite City, Pontoon Beach, South Broadway, the St. Charles/I-370 corridor, Hall Street/North Broadway) got no landmark entry — no single real, named industrial park was confirmed for any of them in this pass, and inventing one would repeat the exact mistake this note already corrects for Moolah Temple. They are real `areas` with no row yet, stated as a gap rather than silently left looking complete. `server/landmarks.js`'s new `distribution-center`/`industrial-plant` categories and real per-capita density (Census CBP NAICS 493110, NAICS 31-33 500+-employee establishments) are what populates an ORDINARY (non-pack) city's warehouse/plant count; a pack-driven city like this one is named real places instead, which is why these four are individually cited rather than counted. FIVE more real, named corporate/industrial locations, by direct instruction ('Walmart's, Targets... Ralston, Purina, Worldwide Technology, Amazon... Procter & Gamble, chemical plants'), each checked individually rather than assumed: Nestlé Purina PetCare's real North American HQ at Checkerboard Square (1 Checkerboard Square, St. Louis — 55 acres, 17 buildings, 'where Ralston Purina Company was founded more than a century ago'; CORRECTED after a direct request to re-check every area's accuracy — first assigned to 'North Riverfront' on no real confirmation at all, then checked and found to be historically at 8th St. between Chouteau Ave. and Gratiot St., with a Downtown St. Louis overview explicitly naming Nestlé Purina PetCare as headquartered in Downtown — moved to 'Downtown', the real area); the real Procter & Gamble home-products plant at 169 E. Grand Ave. (17-acre campus, making Cascade/Mr. Clean/Swiffer/Febreze, operating roughly a century, a real $180M 2024 expansion); the real Solutia W.G. Krummrich chemical plant at 500 Monsanto Ave., Sauget, IL (nearly a century old, formerly operated by Monsanto before its 1997 chemical-business spinoff — the real chemical plant this request asked for by category, not invented); World Wide Technology's real industrial campus near Edwardsville (TriStar-developed, ~176 acres, distinct from WWT's separate real global HQ at 1 World Wide Way, Maryland Heights, MO — the HQ itself got no landmark row here since an office HQ fits neither `distribution-center` nor `industrial-plant` honestly, and 'Maryland Heights' was still added to `areas` as a real place); and a real, named Amazon sortation center in Hazelwood, MO (distinct from the general 'Hazelwood Logistics Center' real-estate park already in this file) — Amazon's other confirmed real Metro East facility (Edwardsville, within Gateway Commerce Center) is covered by the Gateway Commerce Center entry already here rather than duplicated. 'Dierbergs' and 'Schnucks' (real St. Louis-area grocery chains) needed no new row or category — `grocery-store` already exists, generic, real, and unchanged. Walmart/Target/Sam's Club/Costco are the real substance behind `server/landmarks.js`'s new generic `big-box-store` RETAIL_TYPES category rather than a landmark-pack row, the same 'generic category, real density, no brand name' precedent `discount-store` already set for Dollar General/Family Dollar. SIX more real, named logistics facilities, from a direct follow-up ('Amazon's all over the area... 3-4 Edwardsville... East St. Louis, Cahokia Heights area, Sauget area... don't forget the FedExes, UPSs'), each checked rather than assumed: a second, genuinely separate real Amazon building in Edwardsville at 3931 Lakeview Corporate Dr. (confirmed as a distinct real address from the Gateway Commerce Center building already in this file — Amazon's own facility codes for the two disagree across the third-party trackers that track them, so neither code is asserted here, only the real, confirmed street address); a real Amazon 'mini-fulfillment center' in Sauget, IL (confirmed via a real news report, ~200 employees at opening); UPS's real Earth City hub (13818 Rider Trail Dr., per UPS's own careers listings) and a real, smaller UPS delivery center in Belleville, IL (8200 Excellence Place, 36,000 sq ft, 58-truck capacity) — Belleville is a real Metro East city not named directly in this request but genuinely adjacent to Sauget/East St. Louis, added to `areas` for this one real facility; and FedEx Ground's own real Earth City hub (named in FedEx Ground's own hub-location list; no current, confirmed street address was found for it specifically, only a two-decade-old lease record, so none is asserted). Checked and NOT added, stated as a real gap rather than guessed: no confirmed real Amazon, UPS, or FedEx facility address was found specifically in East St. Louis or Cahokia Heights in this pass — only unreliable job-aggregator pages that do not function as real facility records. A real Dec. 2021 St. Louis Business Journal report describes an Amazon lease for a Metro East warehouse but does not name the municipality, so it is not asserted as a specific area's landmark either. FIVE more real business/cultural-district areas and four more real landmarks, by direct instruction ('Add in business areas, Clayton... Westport... U City, which is like our Chinatown... a lot of Indians... St. Ann, Northwest County... a lot of Mexicans... our Bosnian population on the south side... Black American North County, West Side, North Side... South Side'), each checked individually: Clayton (the real St. Louis County seat since 1877/1876 and the county's central business/financial district -- ~70 Fortune 500 HQ/branch offices cited by local coverage) gets the real St. Louis County Government Center (the modern county-government complex in Clayton; sources disagree on the exact address among its several buildings -- 2900/7900 Carondelet, 100 S. Central -- so none is asserted here, only the real complex itself); Westport (Westport Plaza, a real 42-acre mixed-use business/dining/entertainment district in Maryland Heights, opened 1973, 700,000+ sq ft -- genuinely the same immediate area as 'Maryland Heights' above, kept as its own named area since the request named it separately) gets the real Westport Plaza itself. University City gets Jeffrey Plaza (8635 Olive Blvd), a real, specific commercial plaza anchoring the Olive Boulevard corridor that St. Louis Public Radio's own reporting ('Curious Louis: the future of St. Louis' unofficial Chinatown') and local community coverage describe as St. Louis's real, current, informally-recognized Chinese-American commercial district -- the honest match for 'U City, which is like our Chinatown.' CORRECTED rather than asserted as given: St. Louis's actual HISTORIC Chinatown was 'Hop Alley', downtown (roughly 7th/8th and Walnut/Market/Chestnut), real and documented from 1869 until its 1966 demolition for Busch Memorial Stadium's redevelopment area -- a real, significant fact, but about a site that no longer physically exists, so it is named here as historical context rather than given a landmark row that would misrepresent a demolished district as a standing one. CHECKED AND NOT CONFIRMED: no real source found ties a specific Indian-American business corridor to Olive Boulevard specifically -- that corridor's own documented community is Chinese, not Indian; a 2020 analysis (stlmosaicproject.org) does confirm Indian immigrants are real and significant in the broader St. Louis area (having overtaken Mexican immigrants as the area's largest foreign-born group by that measure), but with no specific neighborhood tied to it in what was found, so none is asserted. St. Ann and Overland (Northwest County) are real, confirmed growing Hispanic/Latino communities -- Census-based figures put St. Ann at roughly 12.9% Hispanic (up from 6.9% since the 2020 Census) and Overland at roughly 15.3%, both added to `areas` as real places; no landmark row is forced onto either, since this is a demographic fact about the area rather than a single site. Bevo Mill (the real windmill-style building itself, 4749 Gravois Ave., built 1916 by August Busch Sr. as a halfway stop to Grant's Farm, a City of St. Louis Landmark since 1971, now operating as Das Bevo) is real and is the actual historic anchor of the neighborhood that gives St. Louis's Bosnian community its nickname 'Little Bosnia' -- the St. Louis metro is real and documented as tied with Chicago for the largest Bosnian-American population in the U.S., and as of 2018 was reported to have the largest Bosnian population outside Bosnia-Herzegovina itself (population estimates vary by source, roughly 50,000-70,000, and are named as estimates rather than a census figure). The community has since spread into South St. Louis County (Affton, Mehlville, Oakville per the same sources), which this pack does not have as areas and does not force one for. North St. Louis city and North St. Louis County (including, among others, Ferguson) are real, extensively documented as majority Black American areas -- named here as real geographic/demographic context, the same 'a region is a region, not an invented monument standing in for one' treatment the Ozarks already got above, rather than forcing a landmark onto a broad demographic fact about an area. **None of this demographic color is wired into any mechanic**: this engine's real per-NPC ethnicity system (`ancestryPacks.js`, `africanEthnicGroupPacks.js`) already assigns real Census ancestry data by TRACT POSITION (§88), never by matching a neighborhood's NAME to an ethnicity, and the §9 firewall (`test/ethnicity.test.js`'s own forbidden-file scan) still holds unchanged -- this note's own demographic facts about Clayton/Westport/University City/St. Ann/Overland/Bevo Mill/North St. Louis are real, cited, geographic CONTEXT for the landmark pack, not a new per-NPC rule. EIGHT more real landmarks across four new categories, by direct instruction ('military bases... Scott Air Force Base... Jefferson Barracks... a military or National Guard site off of Goodfellow between Natural Bridge and 70' and 'all the forest information... all the river and lake information'), closing a real gap this project's own VACANCY_CONSOLIDATED_MASTER_SPEC.md names at line 639/642 ('*Strategic:* ...military sites...'; '*Natural:* caves, forests, mountains, rivers, lakes...') and never built beyond caves. Scott Air Force Base is real and genuinely its own census-designated place in St. Clair County, IL, ZIP 62225 — added as its own area ('Scott AFB') rather than forced into the existing 'Belleville' area, since sources name Belleville, O'Fallon, Mascoutah and Shiloh all as real neighboring towns and none as the base's own municipality. Jefferson Barracks is real and still an active Missouri National Guard post (home of the 70th Troop Command, the Guard's largest brigade), in Lemay, MO (a new area) — deactivated as an Army post in 1946, NRHP-listed in 1972, not a historical-only site. Goodfellow Federal Center (4300 Goodfellow Blvd., a new 'Goodfellow / Natural Bridge' area matching the real corridor described) is the real site behind 'a military or National Guard site off of Goodfellow' — a WWII-era Army ammunition plant that today houses real Department of Defense tenants (the Defense Information Systems Agency, the Department of the Army, Defense Finance and Accounting Service-St. Louis), checked directly rather than assumed to be a Guard armory, since no real Guard armory at Goodfellow and Natural Bridge was found in this pass. St. Louis Arsenal (290 Arsenal St., ZIP 63118, South City) is a real, still-active, Air Force-owned installation housing the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency — the other real 'military spot' this pass found checking rather than guessing. The Mississippi and Missouri Rivers are added as real `river` landmarks with NO `area` — both are real, named, major rivers spanning far more than any one of this pack's own neighborhoods, the same honest treatment Meramec Caverns/the Ozarks already got for a real feature too large for one area to hold. Creve Coeur Lake (Maryland Heights, a real natural oxbow lake formed from an old Missouri River meander, the second-largest natural lake in Missouri per the park's own trail map) and Rockwoods Reservation (a new 'Eureka' area, a real 1,843-1,880-acre Missouri Department of Conservation forest dating to 1938) close `lake`/`forest`. No clean national per-capita density figure was found for `military-base`/`forest`/`river`/`lake` (checked, not skipped), so all four stay singleton draws in `server/landmarks.js`, the same honest gap `skyscraper`/`government-building` already declare. TEN more real landmarks, by direct instruction ('every hospital, from the hospital in Belleville, BJC on Kings Highway, all the hospitals... Central West End area to downtown... Fontbonne University... Lincoln University... Harris Stowe University... take the most unusual buildings in the city, similar to how the Civil Courts building... is like one of the eight wonders of the world'), each checked rather than assumed: the Civil Courts Building (Downtown, 1928-1930, Klipstein & Rathmann, a step-pyramid roof modeled on the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World -- a real, documented second downtown courthouse-style building, genuinely distinct from the already-present Old Courthouse); Harris-Stowe State University (3026 Laclede Ave., Midtown, a real public HBCU); Fontbonne University (6800 Wydown Blvd., Clayton) -- CORRECTED from an active university to a `historic-site`: the Board of Trustees voted 10 Mar 2024 to close after the 2025 summer term citing declining enrollment and budget problems, and Washington University purchased the 16-acre campus, so categorizing it as an operating `university` would have the engine auto-hire real faculty at an institution that, as of this pass, no longer operates one; Memorial Hospital Belleville (4500 Memorial Drive, Belleville, IL, a real 398-bed BJC HealthCare acute-care facility) -- the real answer to 'the hospital in Belleville': HSHS St. Elizabeth's, the other Belleville-associated name, actually relocated to O'Fallon, IL in 2017 after 142 years in Belleville, so it is not added as a Belleville landmark; St. Louis Children's Hospital and SSM Health Cardinal Glennon Children's Hospital (Central West End and South City respectively, both real, both ranked nationally); SSM Health DePaul Hospital (Bridgeton, a new area) and Mercy Hospital St. Louis (Creve Coeur, a new area), both real; and the St. Louis VA Medical Center's John Cochran Division (Grand Center, a real VA hospital). CHECKED AND DECLINED: Lincoln University is real and is a real HBCU, but it is in Jefferson City, MO -- roughly 130 miles from St. Louis, its own distinct region entirely -- so it is not added to this pack; forcing it in at a St. Louis-area coordinate would misstate where a real place actually is, the same discipline Meramec Caverns and the Ozarks already got here. Missouri Baptist Medical Center and St. Luke's Hospital (both real, both genuinely in the St. Louis area) are a stated, deliberate gap rather than an oversight -- this pass added the hospitals a direct instruction named or that research surfaced as clearly major, not an exhaustive licensed hospital registry. Confluence Point, asked to be 'a hot spot... a lot of missions... have power': checked directly rather than guessed at, and no code change was needed. Its category, `natural-formation`, is already a hero-tier category (`landmarks.isHeroTier`), so `worldgen.js`'s own pack-driven placement already turns it into a real property with a real `community_id` the identical way every other hero-tier pack entry is placed -- which is the one real precondition `missionTriggers.maybeTriggerMission` checks before it can ever fire there. And the 'hard to open... have the key... hold things on the inside' request for unusual/historic buildings generally is likewise already real and already built, not a new mechanic: `server/hiddenCaches.js` already gives ANY real landmark property (Civil Courts Building and every hospital/university added in this pass included) a real 35% chance of a gated cache needing a real key item, with a further +25% bonus for the historic/religious categories it already names -- built for an earlier, separate direct instruction, and this pass is the confirmation that it already covers what was asked for here too. TWENTY-THREE more real landmarks across two new hero categories and four new retail categories, by direct instruction covering the Piasa Bird/Alton-Grafton docks, breweries, haunted/historic sites, Grant's Farm/Botanical Garden/Tower Grove Park/a second zoo, casinos, stadiums, and big apartment complexes/public housing in one pass: the Piasa Bird (a real, documented Native American legend/mural site on the bluffs near Alton, IL -- added as `historic-site`, no exact street address confirmed, same honest 'no coordinates invented' posture Meramec Caverns already holds) and Grafton Harbor Marina (a real, ~300-combined-slip commercial marina at the Illinois/Mississippi confluence, added as `port-terminal` -- the closest real hero fit for a dock facility, even though it is recreational rather than cargo, stated here rather than left implicit) close the river-dock half of 'anywhere off of any place that touches the Missouri/Mississippi River will have value... people will start to make docks off their homes.' CHECKED AND DEFERRED, not built in this pass: a real mechanic for river-adjacent property value or a 'home dock' transportation bonus needs its own scoping round (what, structurally, makes a property 'touch' a river in this engine) rather than being rushed into a pass that is otherwise pure landmark data. Anheuser-Busch Brewery (1127 Pestalozzi St., Soulard, a new area -- real, one of the largest breweries in the world, `industrial-plant`, the same mega-employer category Procter & Gamble/Solutia already use) closes 'all the breweries... Anheuser-Busch' for the one real brewery that is genuinely a mega-employer industrial plant rather than ordinary commerce. Two real St. Louis craft breweries, Schlafly Tap Room (2100 Locust St., Downtown) and Urban Chestnut Brewing Company (3229 Washington Ave., Midtown), were RESEARCHED AND NOT ADDED as their own rows — the first version of this pass added them as `restaurant`, and `landmark-packs.test.js`'s own real invariant ('a real register holds no hardware stores, and the pack says so') caught it immediately: this hand-typed pack is deliberately restricted to hero-tier heritage places, and `restaurant` is a RETAIL category — ordinary commerce is generated per-area by `worldgen.js`'s own real shop-placement loop, never individually named here, the same reason Dierbergs/Schnucks never got a row either. Named here as a real, citable gap rather than silently dropped. Lemp Mansion (3322 DeMenil Place, Benton Park, a new area -- real, the actual 'old brewery downtown' the request named: the Lemp family's real brewery closed in 1920, and the mansion itself was named one of America's nine most haunted houses by Life magazine in 1980) and the real McPike Mansion equivalent for Alton -- CHECKED AND NOT ADDED as its own row, since the real site found for Alton was the Piasa Bird, already added above; McPike Mansion itself (1861 Alby St.) was researched and is a real, separately citable haunted site this pass did not have room to add as its own row, named here as a gap rather than silently dropped. Grant's Farm (10501 Gravois Rd., Lemay -- real, the historic Busch family estate and animal park, `zoo-aquarium`), Missouri Botanical Garden (4344 Shaw Blvd., a new 'Shaw' area -- real, one of the oldest botanical gardens in the US, a National Historic Landmark) and its real next-door neighbor Tower Grove Park (4256 Magnolia Ave., same Shaw area, donated by the same Henry Shaw in 1868), both added as `park`, the same category Forest Park already uses. 'The zoo off of Riverview' was CHECKED AND NOT CONFIRMED AT THAT EXACT NAME: no real zoo currently operates on Riverview Blvd itself, but the St. Louis Zoo's real, under-construction second campus, WildCare Park ($235M, 425 acres, a new 'Spanish Lake' area in north St. Louis County, the same general north-county corridor Riverview Blvd runs through), is the closest real candidate found and is added as `zoo-aquarium` with this uncertainty stated rather than asserted as a confirmed match. Four real casinos close 'the Maristar, River City Casino, all the casinos' (checked rather than assumed: no casino named 'Maristar' exists; the real, closest-sounding name is Ameristar): River City Casino (Lemay), Ameristar Casino Resort Spa St. Charles (a new 'St. Charles' area), Horseshoe St. Louis (the real current name of the downtown riverfront casino formerly called Lumière Place -- the name the request itself used, corrected to its real current one), and Hollywood Casino St. Louis (Maryland Heights) -- all `casino`, an already-existing hero category (CLAUDE.md's own prior standing rule on the gambling-compliance override), so this closes the DATA half only; the full casino SYSTEM (chips, heavy-composition takeover) stays deferred. 'The Rams Stadium' was CORRECTED rather than added as asked: the Rams left St. Louis for Los Angeles after the 2015 season, and the real building, The Dome at America's Center (formerly the Edward Jones Dome, Downtown), now hosts the UFL's Battlehawks -- added as `stadium-arena` with this history stated. Francis Olympic Field (Washington University, Central West End) is real and closes 'university stadiums' on its own merits -- the oldest Olympic stadium still in continuous use, the main venue for the 1904 Summer Olympics. No real, verified St. Louis-area high-school-stadium capacity ranking was found in this pass (checked, not guessed), so none is added -- a stated gap. Five real apartment complexes close 'big apartment complexes... the Cochrane... O'Fallon Place... the Peabodys... Streets of St. Charles... the Wyndham Chase': checked individually, and the first three turned out to be St. Louis Housing Authority PUBLIC HOUSING developments, not market-rate complexes -- Cochran Plaza (a new 'Columbus Square' area), Clinton-Peabody (Downtown, the real building behind 'the Peabodys'), and Lafayette Townhomes, which SLHA's own listings give as the real current name for the address locally associated with 'O'Fallon Place' -- all three added as the new `apartment-complex` hero category (real `propertyType: 'residential'`, the housing-specific category this request's scale needed rather than forcing public housing into `government-building`). Streets of St. Charles (1650 Beale St., the new St. Charles area) and Windham Chase (12401 Horizon Village Dr., Spanish Lake -- CORRECTED spelling from the request's 'Wyndham Chase', real listings consistently spell it 'Windham') round out the five. 'Countryside' apartments were CHECKED AND NOT FOUND under that name in St. Louis -- a stated gap rather than an invented address. This same research also answers, by direct instruction, 'access to public housing locations... Section 8... spots where Section 8 houses is': individual Section-8/voucher-holder addresses are NOT public data and would raise a real privacy/fair-housing concern to model per-address, the same category of concern this file's own CLAUDE.md already raised declining individual ICE/immigration-status records -- HUD's own Public Housing Developments dataset (project/building-level, not per-household) is the real, honest substitute, and the three SLHA developments named above ARE that dataset's own St. Louis entries, which is why this pass answers both requests with the same three real rows rather than two separate ones. Real vacant/farmland-for-sale data ('look up open land, like farmland... for sale... can be used for farm ground building') was CHECKED AND DECLINED AS A BUILDABLE SOURCE, not silently skipped: no open, structured, national dataset of farmland CURRENTLY FOR SALE exists -- USDA's own Rural Development resale-property file is foreclosure-only and last updated 2018; AcreValue/LandGate/Peoples Company maintain real listings but are private commercial platforms, not open data, and off-market farm sales are the norm rather than the exception per the USDA's own reporting. A real `nursing-home` RETAIL_TYPES category (CMS Nursing Home Compare, ~15,000 Medicare/Medicaid-certified facilities nationally) and `bank`/`gas-station`/`liquor-store` close the national-franchise request ('McDonald's, Subway... franchise banks... QuikTrip, BP, Shell... liquor stores') the same generic-category-over-brand-name way `discount-store`/`big-box-store`/`car-lot` already do -- no brand-named row added for any of these, by design. The real crime-hotspot fact the request itself named ('Speedy on Broadway and Riverview') is real and well-documented under its correct name: the Speedie gas station at North Broadway and Riverview Blvd in the Baden neighborhood, the site of a real December 2022 double killing and a documented 2018 St. Louis Public Radio report on 'armed cruising' along that same corridor -- named here as real geographic/crime CONTEXT, the same posture St. Ann/Overland's demographic facts already hold, and deliberately NOT wired into `crimeHotspotPacks.js` (LA/Chicago only, by that module's own stated scope) or into any escalation mechanic, for the same calibration-risk reason `countryPacks.js`/`regionalTemperamentPacks.js` already stay out of `keys.resolveAggression`. Two real abandoned institutions close 'abandoned hospitals and abandoned schools... St. Alexius... Northwest High School to Walnut Park': the former St. Alexius Hospital (3933 S. Broadway, South City, most recently operating as South City Hospital until its real 2023 closure, now cleared and secured by the city) and the former Northwest High School (5140 Riverview Blvd., a new 'Walnut Park' area -- the real neighborhood the request itself named, and the same Riverview corridor the Speedie gas station and WildCare Park both sit near, closed in 2022 and vacant since) -- both CORRECTED to `historic-site` rather than an active `hospital`/`school`, the same Fontbonne-University correction this pack already made, so the engine does not auto-hire real staff at a building that no longer operates as either. 'An inventory of 70 former public school buildings in STL' (a real, cited source found in this pass) names many more than these two; only the one the request named directly is added, the rest stated as a real, larger gap rather than guessed at individually. Real West St. Louis County Asian population data, by direct instruction ('do the Asian population and how it breaks down in the West County area'): Chesterfield (a new area; 13.79% Asian, ~7,401 residents, 2025 Census-based estimate) and Ballwin (a new area; 9.05% Asian, ~3,042 residents) are the two clearest real West County data points found; St. Louis County's countywide Chinese population (~12,796) is explicitly tied in regional reporting to Clayton, University City, and Chesterfield -- all three already in this pack. CHECKED AND NOT FOUND: a finer real breakdown by specific Asian nationality (Chinese/Indian/Korean/Vietnamese/Filipino) specific to Chesterfield or Ballwin individually, which would need the Census ACS detailed Asian-alone-by-group tables for those two places specifically rather than the city-level totals found here -- stated as the real next step rather than invented. No landmark row is forced onto either area, the same 'a demographic fact about an area, not a site' posture St. Ann/Overland/North St. Louis already hold, and the §9 firewall is unaffected -- this is real, cited geographic context, never a per-NPC rule.
